newsitem.title: USA: Production, talks continue at two GM parts plants.
newsitem.headline: Production, talks continue at two GM parts plants.

text.p: Negotiations between the United Auto Workers and General Motors Corp. continued Monday at two parts plants where union locals dropped last week's strike deadlines and resumed production.
Spokesmen for both the UAW and the automaker characterised the talks as slow at both GM's catalytic converter plant in Oak Creek, Wis., and its metal stamping plant in Grand Rapids, Mich.
"It's slow but it's been productive," Peter Ternes, a spokesman for GM's Grand Rapids plant, said of the talks.
The talks were aimed at resolving disputes over staffing levels, the shifting of work to outside suppliers and long-term business plans.

The union has extended strike deadlines hour-by-hour at the two plants. UAW Local 1866 in Oak Creek had originally set a midnight Thursday deadline, while Local 730 in Grand Rapids had set a midnight Friday deadline.
A strike at either of the two factories could have a significant impact on GM's North American car and truck production.

The Oak Creek plant, near Milwaukee, employs 870 hourly workers and makes exhaust system catalytic converters for nearly all of GM's North American car and truck models. The Grand Rapids plant has 2,346 employees and stamps out sheet metal parts for a variety of GM vehicles, including its all-new minivans.

GM reached a tentative agreement late on Friday for a new local labour contract at a foundry in Saginaw, Mich., averting a threatened strike by about 900 members of UAW Local 445. The foundry produces pistons, piston rods and transmission parts for a variety of GM vehicles.

The two sides continued nearly round-the-clock talks to end an eight-week-old strike by 5,800 workers at GM's Pontiac, Mich., pickup truck plant. Jim Abare, a spokesman for UAW Local 594, said he did not expect an imminent breakthrough in those talks.
GM's stock rose 12.5 cents to $57.375 on the New York Stock Exchange in consolidated late trading.
